researched_by: the council's motorhome guidance page, syndicated North Wales Live reporting (Yahoo News), NRW's Newborough pages and the Bodorgan Estate site
policy_summary:
Anglesey followed Gwynedd's Arosfan model a couple of years behind: in autumn 2025 (reported 5 October 2025) it opened a three-site overnight trial - Holyhead Breakwater Country Park, the Castle (Happy Valley) car park at Beaumaris, and Porth Tyn Tywyn near Rhosneigr - run jointly with Beaumaris Town Council and the Bodorgan Estate. The council's own guidance page calls them 'Arosfan sites, similar to Aires on the continent'. Terms are the tightest in the dataset: GBP10 a night, six vans per site, ONE night only, first-come first-served, self-contained vehicles (onboard toilet and cooking) required, no barbecues, awnings, tables or chairs. The stated aim was to 'reduce the negative impacts seen in areas unable to cope with overnight campervans', naming Aberffraw, Porth Dafarch, Aberlleiniog and Llanddona as problem spots.

The trial was meant to be reviewed after October half-term 2025 but the sites were still listed on the council guidance page in July 2026, with the visitor economy manager describing the scheme as 'under review' in March 2026 after sanitation complaints at Tyn Tywyn - toilet paper and human waste in the dunes, and 30 vans counted at a six-bay site.

The prohibition side is largely landowner-led rather than council TROs: Natural Resources Wales bans all overnight parking (midnight to 6am, GBP100 charge notice, ANPR) across its Newborough National Nature Reserve car parks, and the Bodorgan Estate put height barriers on Porth Trecastell (Cable Bay) in 2024. No published council parking order banning overnight sleeping in ordinary council car parks was found - guidance for the rest of the island is advisory ('avoid parking outside people's houses', get landowner permission off-road).
notes: The trajectory is exclusion first, provision second, from the same actors: the Bodorgan Estate installed height barriers at Porth Trecastell in 2024, then eighteen months later co-ran one of the trial aires at its Porth Tyn Tywyn car park. The trial's one-night limit and six-bay cap look designed to be politically safe rather than to meet demand - 30 vans at Tyn Tywyn on a March day against a six-van cap says the sites are heavily oversubscribed and effectively unenforced, and the dune-fouling complaints that followed are now the main threat to the scheme surviving its review. Newborough - the island's biggest single pressure point - is NRW land, not council, so the strictest regime on Anglesey is entirely outside the council's control.
open_questions: Outcome of the trial review: the sites were still on the council guidance page in July 2026 but no formal decision to make them permanent (or their 2026-season operating dates) was found.
Official scheme name - the council page says 'Arosfan sites', press said 'aires'; one syndicated summary suggested a 'Monfan' brand, which could not be corroborated.

Whether the council's off-street parking order prohibits overnight sleeping in ordinary council car parks (Benllech, Trearddur Bay etc.) - the per-car-park pages are thin templates and no order text was found online.
Beaumaris site postcode discrepancy: council says LL58 8AL, directory listings say LL58 8RA; and whether the pre-trial 12-hour maximum stay was formally lifted for the aire bays.
Original North Wales Live launch article is paywalled; launch details were taken from Yahoo News syndication of the same piece.

sites.name: Holyhead Breakwater Country Park (Arosfan trial site)
sites.search_hint: Breakwater Country Park car park, Holyhead
sites.notes: One of three sites in the autumn 2025 trial, run by the council at its own country park. One night only, first-come first-served, no booking. Self-contained vans (onboard toilet and cooking facilities) required. Trial was 'under review' in March 2026 but still listed on the council guidance page in July 2026.
sites.geocode_precision: country park car park at the base of Holyhead Mountain

sites.name: Castle Car Park (Happy Valley), Beaumaris (Arosfan trial site)
sites.search_hint: Beaumaris Castle / Happy Valley car park, off B5109
sites.notes: Trial aire run in partnership with Beaumaris Town Council. Same terms as the other two sites: GBP10, one night, six vans, self-contained only. Directory listings for the car park pre-trial showed a 12-hour maximum stay and ~GBP6 day charge; how the aire bays interact with day rules is not published. Council gives LL58 8AL, listings LL58 8RA.
sites.geocode_precision: castle car park off the B5109 on the edge of Beaumaris

sites.name: Porth Tyn Tywyn Car Park, near Rhosneigr (Arosfan trial site)
sites.search_hint: Porth Tyn Tywyn beach car park, A4080 between Rhosneigr and Aberffraw
sites.notes: Bodorgan Estate car park run as a trial aire in partnership with the council - the best-equipped of the three (waste point, seasonal toilets) and the most troubled: March 2026 reporting described 30 vans at the six-bay site and human waste in the dunes, with non-self-contained vans using it against the rules. Overnight stays were prohibited here before the trial. Pin is the dune-backed beach car park off the A4080; sources disagree on whether the postcode is LL64 5JR (council) or LL63 5TD.
sites.geocode_precision: beach car park behind the dunes, from plus code 6F8V+9W

sites.name: Newborough National Nature Reserve and Forest car parks (NRW)
sites.notes: Natural Resources Wales land, not council - covers the main beach (Llanddwyn), Airman's and Cwningar car parks, hence no single pin. 'Overnight parking is not allowed for any vehicles. If you park between midnight and 6am you will get a parking charge notice' - GBP100, discounted to GBP60 within 14 days. ANPR barrier plus a mobile attendant; 'no camping - there are official campsites nearby'. The strictest regime on the island, at its single biggest pressure point, and entirely outside the council's control.

sites.name: Porth Trecastell (Cable Bay) Car Park
sites.search_hint: Cable Bay / Porth Trecastell car park, A4080
sites.notes: Bodorgan Estate installed 2.5m frames with swinging height barriers across the entrance in 2024 after persistent overnight motorhome use - physical exclusion of high vehicles rather than signage (schema has no over_height value; over_length used as the closest proxy). Reporting at the time also mentioned restrictions at Cemlyn and Cymyran. The same estate later co-ran the Porth Tyn Tywyn trial aire up the coast.
sites.geocode_precision: beach car park on the A4080 at Cable Bay
